title: Unsupervised Keypoints for Real-Time Fall Detection: Comparative Analysis Under Real-world Conditions with Predictive Bandwidth Reduction
abstract: arXiv:2607.15400v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Falls among older adults are a major safety and health-systems challenge, yet continuous in-person monitoring is difficult to sustain across home and clinical care settings. Video-based monitoring can capture fall-relevant motion, but scalable real-time deployment is limited by privacy, compute, and bandwidth constraints, and existing keypoint-based methods typically rely on supervised or anatomical pose representation, which is vulnerable to occlusion and partial body visibility. We propose a fall-monitoring framework that replaces continuous video transmission with compact motion representations, using unsupervised keypoints which are extracted locally, and a variational recurrent model is used to forecast motion at the staff end, followed by fall classification. translated_title: 基于无监督关键点的实时跌倒检测：真实世界条件下的对比分析与预测性带宽削减
translated_abstract: 老年人跌倒是重大的安全和医疗系统挑战，然而在家庭和临床护理环境中持续进行人工监护难以维持。基于视频的监控能够捕捉与跌倒相关的运动，但可扩展的实时部署受到隐私、计算和带宽限制的制约，且现有的基于关键点的方法通常依赖监督式或解剖学姿态表示，容易受到遮挡和部分身体可见性的影响。我们提出了一种跌倒监测框架，用以替代连续视频传输的是紧凑的运动表示：该框架使用在本地提取的无监督关键点，并在护理人员端采用变分循环模型预测运动，随后进行跌倒分类。我们在UR Fall和Human Fall数据集上，采用随机划分、受试者不交叉划分和基于遮挡的划分对该框架进行评估，以系统地刻画每种条件下的表现。
tldr: 该论文提出一种基于本地提取的无监督关键点与变分循环运动预测的跌倒监测框架，以紧凑运动表示替代连续视频传输，从而降低带宽需求、保护隐私并增强对遮挡情况的鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a fall-monitoring framework that replaces continuous video transmission with locally-extracted unsupervised keypoints and variational recurrent motion forecasting, reducing bandwidth requirements while improving robustness to occlusion and partial body visibility.
